Subject: Residency & retention questions for HIPAA workflow

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this. We are evaluating Redwood Private for a PHI workflow and have a couple of time-sensitive questions for procurement and security before we move to legal (deadline: 2026-05-20):

- Can Redwood guarantee data residency in a US-only region (we prefer us-east) for all customer data, including logs, KV cache, and embeddings?
- What are the configurable retention limits for raw message content, embeddings, and system logs? Do you offer immediate deletion APIs? What is the expected end-to-end deletion SLA (including backups)?
- What redaction options do you support for PII/PHI (pre-send client-side, on-ingest deterministic redaction, tokenization, field encryption, etc.)? Any recommended patterns for minimizing PHI egress while still using generation/embedding features?
- Are SOC 2 reports and a HIPAA BAA available? Any evidence we can provide our auditors quickly?

We'd like a short written response and any artifacts you can share (SOC2 summary, redaction options matrix). Happy to book a call if useful.

Best,
Amelia Turner
Director, Security & Compliance
CarePoint Health

From: Redwood Inference <support@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Residency, retention, and redaction — CarePoint PHI question

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear questions. Summary answers below and attached artifacts. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk the team through options.

1) Data residency
- Redwood Private can be deployed into a customer VPC or into a region-specific account we manage for you; both options allow guaranteed US-only residency (we can lock to us-east-1). All persistent customer data (objects, databases, KV cache, embeddings) can be restricted to the selected region.

2) Retention limits and deletion
- Configurable retention per data class: message content (default 30 days; configurable to any value down to 0 days), embeddings (default 90 days; configurable down to 1 day with caveats), and system/application logs (default 90 days; configurable to 7 days minimum for operational telemetry).
- Immediate deletion APIs: yes — we expose a Tenant Delete API that marks data for deletion immediately. Final destruction process: primary store deletion occurs within minutes; background jobs purge derivative stores and indexes; removal from snapshots/backups is performed according to backup retention policy but we provide an accelerated purge that completes within an SLA window.
- Deletion SLA: standard accelerated purge SLA is 72 hours for final removal from all actively served stores and indexes; artifacts in long-term immutable backups require a separate agreement (we can include a backup purge clause in the BAA/contract).

3) Redaction and PHI minimization options
- Client-side pre-send redaction: recommended when you can remove PHI before it leaves your network. We provide SDK helpers and patterns for deterministic tokenization/hashing on the client.
- Server-side on-ingest deterministic masking: Redwood can apply ingestion hooks that mask or redact configured fields (names, SSNs, MRNs) before indexing or embedding. Masking is deterministic so it preserves referential integrity when required.
- Field-level encryption: for sensitive structured attributes, use our field-level encryption (customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM). Encrypted fields are opaque to model processing unless explicitly decrypted by your application.
- Tokenization & pseudonymization for embeddings: we recommend hashing or tokenizing PHI prior to embedding; if you need semantic embeddings, consider a two-stage approach — embed only de-identified context and store a reversible token map inside your protected key store.
- Differential retention approach: keep minimal context (short-lived) for generation features and move richer long-term records into an audit-only store with stricter access controls.

4) Compliance artifacts and integrations
- SOC 2 Type II summary attached (SOC2_Summary_v2.pdf).
- We offer a HIPAA BAA; draft template attached (BAA_template.docx) — legal can iterate.
- We integrate with customer KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and provide audit logs with token-level access traces.

5) Implementation timeline
- Standard Private deployment + region lock: 3–5 business days (depends on VPC setup).
- Redaction hooks and client-side SDK helpers: typically 1–2 sprints to implement and test (2–4 weeks) depending on scope.
- Accelerated backup purge clause: addendum during contracting; delivery time varies by contract negotiation.

Attachments: redaction-options-matrix.xlsx (filled with recommended patterns), SOC2_Summary_v2.pdf, BAA_template.docx

-----END DRAFT-----
